title: Acceleration & Strength
summary: Fully cleared and back running. Pogos are back in. Broad jumps are on hold for a later block, so they're swapped for box jumps. Calf work is the most useful thing for the ankle.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
exercises.cue: Injured side as front leg: let the knee drift forward over the toes slowly. If the front of the ankle pinches, stop short of it.

exercises.name: Calf Raises (double then single leg)
exercises.cue: 2×10 double-leg, then 2×10 single-leg on the injured side. Primes the calf before pogos. If single-leg reps are clearly worse than the good side, keep pogos easy.

exercises.name: Pogo Jumps
exercises.cue: Start low and quick (ankles stiff, heels just off the ground), then build height across sets. Land quietly, even left and right. Stop the set if he lands flat-footed or favours one side.

exercises.name: Falling Start Accels
exercises.cue: Build from about 70% effort on the first rep, then go full.

exercises.name: Box Jump (instead of Broad Jump)
exercises.cue: Jump up, step down. Same power intent, no horizontal landing.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
exercises.cue: Held for a later block. Comes back via box jumps, then broad jumps with a 2-second stuck landing.

exercises.name: DB Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.cue: Injured leg as the front leg: control the knee travel forward rather than dropping into the bottom.

exercises.name: DB Calf Raise (single leg)
exercises.cue: The most useful exercise in the session for the ankle. Single-leg, slow 3-second lower, full range.

exercises.name: Split Stance Cable Pallof Press
exercises.cue: Do sets with each leg in front.

next: Pogos: 15 → 20 reps, then forward/back and side-to-side pogos, then single-leg pogos.
Broad jumps: box jumps → broad jump with a 2-second stuck landing → full broad jumps.
Ready for broad jumps when pogos feel easy and even, sprints are pain-free, and he can do about 25 single-leg calf raises on the injured side.
